newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian finance minister gets good reception.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian finance minister gets good reception.

text.p: Latvia's financial sector and Western analysts welcomed the appointment of new finance minister Robert Zile on Thursday, calling him a reform-minded man who should manage the country's finances well.

"I think he has demonstrated the ability to be a good manager of the finance committee of parliament," stock exchange president Uldis Cerps told Reuters."I think he is a convinced reformer." The 38-year old Zile, the former head of parliament's finance and budget committee, is stepping into a controversial government post that has been vacant since October and caused the previous government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele to fall.

Shkele quit in January after President Guntis Ulmanis asked parliament to reject Shkele's proposed finance minister. Since then, Shkele and the president have come to terms on their differences, and Shkele formed a new government that took office two weeks ago. Zile has been in politics since the movement began to regain Latvia's independence from the former Soviet Union in the 1980s and is a member of the third-largest party in the eight-party coalition, For Fatherland and Freedom.
But in his new position, Zile will need to ensure Latvia meets a balanced budget.

The balanced budget is a key part of Shkele's economic policy, launched after he came to power at the end of 1995. Shkele, a non-party businessman, has said his main aim is to sort out Latvia's economy, badly damaged by a bank crisis in mid-1995, and speed up privatisation. Zile, an economist who has studied in the U.S., Canada and Australia, has said there are no concerns about meeting the balanced 1997 budget and backed drafting of another deficit-free fiscal package for 1998. "Zile is a professional, an economist, which is extremely important for a finance minister," said Ivar Kirsons, vice-president of Unibanka.

"He understands both the macroeconomic situation and has experience in the formation of a budget," Kirsons added. "I am very pleased with this appointment, he is a man with his heart and mind in the right place," said one senior Western financial expert. "I do not know how good a manager he is, but he is definetely the best choice in the circumstances."
